purpose: Provide explicit and auditable provenance for architectural knowledge used by the design-time Architecture RAG.

provenance_policy.peer_reviewed_literature: The core concept represented by the knowledge entry is directly supported by a scholarly peer-reviewed source.
provenance_policy.SWIM_or_domain_source: The knowledge entry is grounded primarily in the SWIM exemplar or another system/domain-specific source.
provenance_policy.research_design_decision: The knowledge entry represents an explicit design choice made for this research architecture and must not be presented as if it were directly prescribed by literature.
provenance_policy.prototype_engineering_rule: The knowledge entry represents an implementation-specific engineering rule of the prototype.
provenance_policy.mixed_provenance: The knowledge entry combines literature-supported concepts with research-specific synthesis, constraints, or mechanisms.

research_design_decisions.description: The demonstrator deliberately considers centralized, decentralized, and hybrid control structures as alternative architecture choices so that control topology is exposed as a design decision rather than fixed implicitly.
Generative LLM reasoning is separated from deterministic runtime authority. Candidate adaptations must pass an independently implemented deterministic safety check before effectors may be invoked.
Agentic replanning is intentionally bounded so autonomous recovery cannot continue indefinitely; exhausted recovery transfers control to fail-safe handling and escalation.

The LLM and automated design workflow provide decision support only. Final architecture approval remains with the human architect, and unresolved runtime recovery is escalated rather than autonomously overriding trusted authority.
Post-execution outcomes are represented as PASS, PARTIAL, or FAIL using observed managed-system state. PARTIAL indicates successful actuation without yet restoring the adaptation goal.

Candidate architectures are scored from 1 to 5 for architect-selected quality attributes and combined using architect-defined numerical weights. The weighted mechanism is a demonstrator-specific decision-support implementation and must not be described as the ATAM method itself.
The prototype records adaptation states, diagnoses, candidate plans, safety verdicts, execution outcomes, and recovery information in a runtime knowledge base for later retrieval and analysis.

The demonstrator applies retrieval-augmented generation specifically to software-architecture design by retrieving curated architectural knowledge before LLM-supported alternative generation, trade-off reasoning, validation, and reconsideration. This is a research-specific application of the broader RAG concept.

The demonstrator records the selected architecture, alternatives, rationale, and consequences in an explicit architecture-decision artifact so that human approval and later reconsideration remain traceable.
